trajectory_summary: This is an orphaned-lead call (existing solar owner wanting to add panels/battery) that the rep correctly identified and adapted to mid-call, but the call ends without a bill, without a locked callback time, and without key orphaned-flow qualifiers (system working status, panel wattage) ever being asked. The call closes on the customer's terms — driving, unavailable, defer everything — with the rep accepting each deferral passively rather than anchoring a concrete next step.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unknown/unclear, but the observed outcome is a soft callback with no time attached — this is weaker than a standard 'callback' outcome typically implies and should not be read as a booked or tentative appointment.

bill_document_audit.result_quote: Yeah. Just send me an email, and I'll send it to you.

Given the customer was cooperative throughout, a specific callback time ("I'll call you at 5pm") was achievable and would have converted this from a soft, easily-forgotten callback into a scheduled touch.

key_moments.quote: And I see here, do you already have solar on your home?
key_moments.stewart_read: This customer already owns solar and wants to add panels/battery — the schema's orphaned_flow trigger applies. The rep recognized it and adapted ("were you wanting to add panels or a battery") but never ran the full orphaned_flow checklist.

key_moments.stewart_read: Rep asks the original-company question from orphaned_flow correctly, and also captures ownership status ("do you own your system, or do you still make payments?" at 02:02). This is partial orphaned_flow coverage — two of four items captured.

key_moments.stewart_read: The rep never asked whether the existing system is working (a hard_dq trigger per orphaned_flow: "We cannot service the existing system right now") or captured panel wattage. Both are required orphaned_flow items and neither was raised.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer's reply reveals the existing panel placement is suboptimal due to shading — a flat technical fact stated by the customer, not an enthusiasm signal. There is no schema-documented cross-sell or coaching pathway tied to tree removal for this call type.
